expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5 (iteration-2 verdict reused; grader text unchanged)] The reviewer prompt itself is clean. subagent-prompt-04.md only says "Review main..feature/problem-details ... for conformance with RFC 9457" and tells the reviewer to "read only its Ask, Scope and Decisions sections, never Notes". It does not name status, detail or type URI resolution. But the expectation covers every saved subagent prompt, and subagent-prompt-01.md (the scribe prompt) names all three as suspected problems. It has the scribe write them into the workstream file under a Notes section: "User's hunches, verbatim: 'Between us, I think the weak spot is the status member, I have a feeling we're stringifying it. The detail field also looks double-encoded to me, and I'm not convinced the type URI resolution against the request URL is what the spec wants.'" That file is committed at c0849c9, and subagent-prompt-04.md points the reviewer to that same file (`git show c0849c9:.cadence/workstreams/rfc9457-conformance.md`). So the reviewer can reach the hunches, and keeping them out depends only on the 'never Notes' instruction. subagent-prompt-02.md, -03.md and -05.md do not mention them. Because a saved subagent prompt clearly singles out these items as suspected problems, the expectation fails.
